name: Cannibalism
overview: Scripture acknowledges the reality of cannibalism as a dire consequence of judgment and distress, as seen in Leviticus 26:29 and Deuteronomy 28:53-54, where eating the flesh of one's own children is described as a horrific result of God's discipline during siege and hardship. While Genesis 9:3 grants permission for humans to eat animals, the Bible distinctly warns against adopting pagan practices, including those connected with idolatry and occultism (Deuteronomy 12:30, 18:10), which can be linked to such abominable acts. Thus, the biblical witness presents cannibalism not as normative but as a tragic sign of covenantal failure and divine judgment.
